statements.impact_statement: CVE-2021-4214 is a heap overflow in pngimage.c, a test program in libpng's source tree that is not part of the library (https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng/issues/302). The libpng maintainer describes pngimage.c there as an internal test program not meant to be used by external users, and Debian rates the CVE unimportant because the crash is in a program not shipped in its binary packages (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2021-4214). We unpacked all 10 binary packages published from the libpng1.6 source in the DHI Debian repository: a single build, a rebuild of Debian 1.6.48-1+deb13u6, for amd64 and arm64, made up of libpng16-16t64, libpng-dev, libpng-tools and the libpng16-16t64 and libpng-tools debug symbol packages. None ships a pngimage program, and no installed file other than the upstream change log mentions pngimage. The ELF files are libpng16.so.16 and the pngfix and png-fix-itxt tools, all dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, plus the separate debug files in the debug symbol packages, which do not mention pngimage either; libpng-dev also has the libpng16-config shell script. libpng-dev also ships the static archive libpng16.a, whose members are the library's own objects: png.c, pngerror.c, pngget.c, pngmem.c, pngpread.c, pngread.c, pngrio.c, pngrtran.c, pngrutil.c, pngset.c, pngtrans.c, pngwio.c, pngwrite.c, pngwtran.c and pngwutil.c, plus intel_init.c and filter_sse2_intrinsics.c on amd64, or arm_init.c, filter_neon_intrinsics.c and palette_neon_intrinsics.c on arm64. libpng-dev's examples directory holds the example.c and pngtest.c sources and pngtest.png, not pngimage.c. pngimage.c is not built into any shipped binary.
